device.name: iQOO Z7s
device.cpu_features: NEON, ARM_FMA, FP16_VA, DOTPROD, LLAMAFILE, OPENMP, KLEIDIAI, REPACK

key_finding.title: KleidiAI accelerates only Q4_0 and Q8_0 - not the K-quants
key_finding.evidence: llama.cpp emits: 'kleidiai: no kernel for tensor type q4_K, not accelerated by KleidiAI (kernels available for Q4_0 and Q8_0)'
key_finding.implication: The most widely shipped mobile quantization (Q4_K_M) misses the Arm-optimized kernels entirely. Staying inside {Q4_0, Q8_0} is worth ~3x on time-to-first-token on this SoC.
key_finding.measured: Q8_0 prefill 67.4 t/s and Q4_0 49.2 t/s vs Q4_K_M 29.3 t/s (cool device, isolated runs)

uniform_baselines.note: Isolated runs on a cool device. Perplexity chunk counts differ between sweeps and are labelled per entry; only compare ppl at equal chunks.

search.objective: minimise on-disk size subject to perplexity <= Q4_K_M reference (the popular default), over per-layer precision in {Q4_0, Q8_0} - every candidate stays on KleidiAI-accelerated kernels

anvil.config: layers 10-17 -> Q4_0, all other layers + token_embd -> Q8_0

greedy.note: no feasible configuration found within the same 14-evaluation budget

random.note: no feasible configuration found within the same 14-evaluation budget

head_to_head.note: Anvil's winning config vs the Q4_K_M default, quantized and benchmarked back-to-back on a cooled device (the fair comparison).

summary.generation_cost: -31% sustained tokens/sec (larger model is more bandwidth-bound per token)

frontier_sweep.note: Exhaustive k-sweep over the same axis Anvil searched: protect the k most quant-sensitive layers at Q8_0, leave the rest at Q4_0. Measured at 4 perplexity chunks, same as the search. Feasibility bar = Q4_K_M reference ppl 9.605.
conclusions: Anvil's searched configuration (k=20) is the SMALLEST feasible point on the measured frontier - the search landed on the optimum, not merely near it.

The frontier is non-monotonic (k=16 is worse than k=12; k=24 worse than k=20). Protecting more layers does not reliably improve quality - WHICH layers are protected matters. This is a direct argument for measurement-driven search over any fixed heuristic, though part of the wobble is 4-chunk perplexity noise.

Uniform Q4_0 (k=0, 945 MiB, ppl 10.508) is worse quality than Q4_K_M at essentially the same size (935 MiB, ppl 9.605) - so simply switching to the KleidiAI-fast type is not enough on its own. The per-layer mix is what recovers the quality while keeping the fast kernels.
Mapping this frontier cost 8 on-device evaluations (33.7 min); Anvil reached the same optimum inside its 14-evaluation budget while also measuring off-axis configurations.

tensor_granularity_probe.note: Can per-TENSOR protection (cheaper than per-layer: attn_v/attn_k are 0.75 MiB vs ffn_* at 26.25 MiB) reach the Q4_K_M quality bar at Q4_K_M's size, using only KleidiAI-accelerated types? Base Q4_0, listed tensors promoted to Q8_0, token_embd pinned Q8_0. 4 perplexity chunks.
tensor_granularity_probe.conclusion: NEGATIVE RESULT, and the most useful one. At 951-1140 MiB no arrangement of Q4_0/Q8_0 comes close to Q4_K_M's 9.605. The default's advantage is not WHICH tensors it protects - it is that K-quants carry better quality-per-bit (super-block scales). Tensor-level protection cannot recover it. Combined with the layer sweep, 14 matched-setting measurements (all at 4 perplexity chunks) establish that the accelerated-format coverage - not the search - is the binding constraint.

thermal_instability_finding.headline: On this class of mid-range mobile silicon, on-device LLM speed benchmarks are NOT reproducible without bracketed reference controls. We measured up to -44% drift in a single 25-minute session.
thermal_instability_finding.why_it_matters: Any mobile LLM benchmark reporting bare tokens/sec without a thermal control is unreliable. We report this as a methodology contribution because it invalidates a class of comparisons other work performs casually - including, initially, our own.

session_A_37min.note: Sequence is non-monotonic - it bounces rather than decaying, so the variation is not simple thermal decay.

session_B_25min.note: Same reference configuration, same device, same binary. A -44% swing inside one session.

reproduced_low_readings.note: Both re-measured and reproduced, but with the reference itself unstable we cannot attribute these to the configurations rather than to the environment.

thermal_instability_finding.consequence_for_this_work: We DO NOT publish a quality-vs-latency Pareto frontier over accelerated configurations - the environment cannot support that granularity. Speed claims are made only from a single isolated, cooled, within-session comparison. Quality and size results are unaffected because perplexity and file size are deterministic and thermally invariant.
thermal_instability_finding.recommended_practice: Bracket every mobile inference benchmark with a fixed reference configuration measured before and after; report the drift; discard sessions exceeding a pre-declared threshold. Our bench_frontier_z7s.py implements this control.

speed_evidence_used.note: The ONLY speed comparison we make headline claims from: three uniform formats, one isolated cooled session, no drift confound.
speed_evidence_used.conclusion: Prefill speed tracks kernel availability, not bit-width: the 8-bit accelerated model is 2.3x faster than the 4.5-bit unaccelerated one, and the 4-bit accelerated model is 1.68x faster. Fewer bits does not mean faster prefill on this device - having a kernel does.

measurement_variance_disclosure.issue: Q4_K_M prefill measured 29.3 t/s in an isolated cool run and 17.9 t/s in the back-to-back comparison session. The Snapdragon 695 throttles, so ABSOLUTE tokens/sec drifts between sessions.
measurement_variance_disclosure.policy: Only WITHIN-SESSION ratios are treated as reliable. Cross-session absolute values are reported but never used to form a headline ratio.

anvil_vs_q4km_ttft_ratio.reported_range: 1.8x - 2.9x depending on thermal state; the 1.8x figure is the conservative floor and is the one we lead with in any single-number claim.

kernel_value_counterfactual.question: If Arm added a Q4_K KleidiAI kernel, how much would it actually help? Answered from measured data, no new experiment required.
kernel_value_counterfactual.method: Q4_0 (KleidiAI-accelerated, 886 MiB) and Q4_K_M (not accelerated, 935 MiB) are comparable-bit-width 4-bit formats measured in the SAME cool session. Their prefill ratio isolates the acceleration headroom available to a 4-bit format on this silicon.

measured_headroom.interpretation: The existing Q4_0 kernel already demonstrates a 1.68x uplift over the unaccelerated path for a 4-bit format on this device.

engineering_specification.target: A Q4_K kernel would need approximately 1.7x - 1.8x over the current unaccelerated Q4_K_M path to reach parity with the best KleidiAI-accelerated configuration we measured.
engineering_specification.projected_outcome: Q4_K_M would move from 29.3 to ~49 t/s prefill while retaining its 935 MiB size and 9.605 perplexity - dominating Anvil's best accelerated config (1386 MiB, 9.522) on size at comparable speed.
engineering_specification.consequence: That single kernel would collapse the quality-vs-latency trade-off mobile developers face today.
engineering_specification.caveat: K-quant dequantization is inherently more complex than Q4_0 (super-block scales), and Q4_K_M also contains Q6_K tensors that equally lack kernels, so full parity with Q4_0 may not be attainable. 1.68x is the demonstrated headroom for the simpler format, treated here as an optimistic bound.

kernel_value_counterfactual.evidence_base: 14 measurements at matched 4-chunk perplexity: 8-point layer-granularity frontier, 4-point tensor-granularity probe, F16 reference, Q4_K_M reference. Exploratory 10-chunk perplexities and speed benchmarks are reported separately and never mixed with these.

claim_scope.note: Deliberately narrow wording. Our measurements cover ONE model (Qwen2.5-1.5B) on ONE Arm device (Snapdragon 695) with ONE runtime (llama.cpp build 10354).
claim_scope.supported_claim: For the tested Arm mobile configuration, KleidiAI accelerates Q4_0/Q8_0 paths but not Q4_K_M; a 14-measurement study at matched settings shows Q4_0/Q8_0 tensor selection cannot reproduce Q4_K_M's quality at comparable model size.
claim_scope.not_claimed: We do NOT claim this generalises to every Arm device, every model, or the entire mobile LLM ecosystem. Q4_K_M's status as a widely used default is context, not a measured result of this work.

live_demo.command: llama-cli -m anvil_best.gguf -t 4 -p "Explain why quantizing a neural network makes it faster, in two sentences." -n 80
live_demo.reported_speed: prompt 33.9 t/s, generation 5.4 t/s (llama-cli, warm device)

caveats: The Snapdragon 695 throttles under sustained load; a benchmark taken immediately after ~2h of continuous quantization read 22.7 t/s prefill for the same config that reads 52.6 t/s on a cooled device. All headline numbers are from cooled, back-to-back runs.
llama-bench generation (tg) numbers carry high variance on this SoC (stddev up to ~1.8 t/s); prefill (pp) is far more stable.
Search used 4 perplexity chunks to fit the evaluation budget; the F16 and Q4_K_M references were measured at the same 4 chunks so the comparison is like-for-like.
Anvil's per-layer sensitivity prior (outer layers matter more) seeds the surrogate; it is calibrated online from measured perplexity.
